# Intake Brief — Move level label to left (MS-0MUGRKEWZ0073327)

## Problem Statement
When a business or community-space card is upgraded it shows a gold level badge
("Lvl 1", "Lvl 2", …) in the **top-right** corner of the card face. This
position competes with the cost circle / right-hand text column and reads as a
secondary stat rather than the card's primary upgrade indicator. The badge
should move to the **top-left** of the card so the upgrade level is immediately
visible in a consistent, expected position.

## Users
- **Main Street player** — wants to identify an upgraded card's level at a
  glance when scanning the street grid and their hand.
- **Future example-game authors / designers** — reuse the shared
  `UpgradeOverlaySpec` contract and expect a single, predictable corner
  convention for the level badge.

### User Stories
- As a player, when I look at an upgraded card on the street or in my hand, I
  see the "Lvl N" badge at the top-left of the card, so the level is obvious at
  a glance.
- As a player, the badge position is identical whether the card is shown on the
  street grid or in the hand, so I never have to re-learn where to look.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] For every upgraded card (`level > 0`), the level badge is positioned at
      the card's **top-left**: in container-local coordinates (origin at the
      card centre) `levelBadge.x` is negative (left of centre) and the badge is
      **left-anchored** (`originX === 0`); the badge is no longer placed in the
      top-right (`x` must not be positive in the mirrored position). Verified by
      unit test on `buildUpgradeOverlaySpec` for level 1 and level 2 cards.
- [ ] The Phaser renderer (`applyUpgradeOverlays`) renders the badge with a
      left/top origin so the text starts at the top-left inset and remains fully
      inside the card bounds (no clipping past the left or top edge); the same
      overlay path is used by street and hand cards, so both move together.
      Verified by renderer/overlay tests.
- [ ] Badge content and styling are unchanged (`Lvl N`, gold `#ffdd44`, bold,
      10px) and no badge is produced for level 0 (base) cards.
- [ ] The dynamic SVG card-face generator (`generateBusinessCardSvg`) emits the
      level badge at the top-left (`x` at the card's left inset,
      `text-anchor="start"`) for consistency with the overlay, with its unit
      tests updated accordingly.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
      (notably the module docs in `UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` /
      `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` and the level-badge references in
      `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes, with all existing
      top-right level-badge expectations updated to the top-left contract.

## Constraints
- Card geometry is fixed: canonical **140 × 80** card with a **64 × 64 art zone
  at (8, 8)** (top-left) — see `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md`. The
  top-left corner is therefore occupied by the card art; the badge will render
  over the top-left of the art zone (mirroring the current badge overlaying the
  top-right). This is an accepted input to the brief (see Risks & Assumptions).
- Presentation-only change — no change to upgrade rules, card state, or level
  numbers.
- Reuse the existing overlay/badge primitives and gold styling; do not introduce
  new assets or a second badge component.
- Keep the overlay spec a pure data module (no Phaser imports) so it stays
  unit-testable in Node.

## Existing State
- `src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` builds the badge at
  `x = Math.round(width / 2 - 4)`, `y = Math.round(4 - height / 2)` (top-right,
  4 px inset) with `color: '#ffdd44'`, `fontSize: '10px'`, `fontStyle: 'bold'`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` (`applyUpgradeOverlays`) creates the
  Phaser Text and calls `lvlText.setOrigin(1, 0)` — right/top anchored — so the
  badge sits in the top-right.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`generateBusinessCardSvg`) emits
  `<text x="${width - 8}" y="13" … text-anchor="end">Lvl N</text>` (top-right)
  for upgraded cards. (This dynamic SVG path is exercised by unit tests; the
  runtime card face texture comes from the CSV-based template SVGs.)
- Tests asserting/pinning the badge: `tests/main-street/upgraded-card-rendering.test.ts`
  (positions the badge in the top-right), `tests/main-street/upgrade-overlay-spec.test.ts`
  and `tests/main-street/cash-line-overlay.test.ts` (badge presence/text),
  `tests/main-street/card-svg-generator.test.ts` (badge text).

## Desired Change
- Mirror the badge to the top-left: overlay `x = Math.round(-width / 2 + 4)`
  with `originX: 0` (and `setOrigin(0, 0)` in the renderer); `y` stays at the
  existing top inset so the badge remains on the top edge.
- Update the SVG generator badge to `x = 8` (or the chosen left inset) with
  `text-anchor="start"`.
- Update the module/JSDoc comments and the affected tests from "top-right" to
  "top-left". Exact inset values may be tuned during implementation as long as
  the badge is left-anchored in the top-left and stays inside the card bounds.

## Key Files
- `src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` — level-badge spec `x` / `originX` and the
  "top-right corner" comment; primary change.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — `applyUpgradeOverlays` badge
  `setOrigin(1, 0)` → `(0, 0)`; comment.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — dynamic SVG badge position /
  `text-anchor`; module doc mentions "level badge top-right".
- `tests/main-street/upgraded-card-rendering.test.ts` — update the top-right
  position assertion to top-left and assert left-anchoring.
- `tests/main-street/upgrade-overlay-spec.test.ts` — badge position/style
  expectations.
- `tests/main-street/cash-line-overlay.test.ts` — badge presence/absence
  alongside the cash line (position regression surface).
- `tests/main-street/card-svg-generator.test.ts` — SVG badge text/position.
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — level-badge placement references.

## Related Work
- **Potentially related docs:**
  - `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — canonical 140×80 card and the
    `(8, 8)` 64×64 art zone that occupies the top-left.
  - `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — upgrade level-up burst notes that
    reference the newly-rendered level badge.
  - `src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` header — documents the overlay contract
    and the card-local coordinate system.
- **Potentially related work items:**
  - `MS-0MTV69NII000LW8I` — *Position end-turn coin matrix on left side of card,
    growing right* (bug, medium) — closest precedent: a card-face overlay
    repositioned from centre/right to left, landed with documented placement
    assumptions.
  - `MS-0MU9JYNZ3008AH5J` — *Update createCoinGrid defaults to left-anchored
    position* (task) — companion implementation task for the sister reposition.
  - `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E` — *Assign a dedicated 64×64 sprite to every Main
    Street card* (medium) — touches the top-left art zone that the badge will
    now overlay.
  - `MS-0MTRRYOT6001167R` — *Change the name of Physiotherapy business card to
    Physiotherapist* (task, low) — another card-face presentation tweak with
    test/doc churn.
  - Historical (core-repo) references cited in code: `CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN`
    (64×64 left-art layout) and `CG-0MP1VJVEK003I7VE` (display upgrade state on
    street-grid cards) — the layout and overlay these tests assert were
    introduced/refined there.
- **Automated report** (generated by `find-related`) — see the
  "Related work (automated report)" section retained below.

## Risks & Assumptions
- **Assumption:** "top left" means the card's top-left corner, mirroring the
  current right-side inset, with the badge left-aligned. Because the 64×64 art
  zone occupies `(8, 8)`–`(72, 72)`, the badge will overlay the top-left of the
  card art. That is accepted; if the producer finds it illegible over the art, a
  subtle backing chip or a slightly different inset is a small follow-up — it
  must be raised rather than assumed.
- **Visual-regression risk:** the badge colour (`#ffdd44` gold) may have low
  contrast against some card art; mitigate during implementation by checking the
  darkest/lightest card arts and, if needed, a 1 px dark outline (recorded as a
  follow-up if it expands scope).
- **Test churn:** `upgraded-card-rendering.test.ts` explicitly asserts a
  top-right position; update the assertions to the top-left contract in the same
  change rather than deleting them.
- **Scope creep:** do not restyle the badge, redesign the 64×64 layout, or
  change the cost circle / title / cash line. Record any broader card-face polish
  as separate work items.

## Open Questions
- None — the seed context (position the upgrade level badge at the top-left
  instead of the top-right) plus repo inspection of the overlay/spec/renderer
  provided sufficient signal for a clear brief. The only judgement call (badge
  overlays the top-left art zone) is recorded above as an assumption to be
  confirmed during review; no clarifying interview was required.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers
- No interview conducted — the work-item description ("When a card is upgraded
  it gets a 'Lvl 1' label. Move this from the current location (top right) to
  the top left.") plus repo inspection of `UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts`,
  `MainStreetRendererStreet.ts`, and `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` provided
  sufficient signal to draft a clear brief. No assumptions were left
  unrecorded; see Risks & Assumptions for the documented top-left-art-overlay
  assumption.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV** – write storylines (open)
- **MS-0MTIILDBB001F01S** – Competitive Monte Carlo harness: head-to-head simulation (blocked)
- **MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M** – Implement IT Specialist and Delivery Driver cost-reduction effects (open)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: card, current, gets, label, left, level, location, lvl, move, right, top, upgraded, when
- `core/docs/the-build/genre-research.md` — matched: card, current, gets, left, level, location, move, right, top, upgraded, when
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: card, current, gets, label, left, level, move, right, top, upgraded, when

# Intake Brief: Render the storyline graph (Mermaid to SVG) in the docs build (MS-0MUNB54KU005084C)

**Priority: High** | **Type: Chore** | **Assignee: Map**

> Discovered from the "write storylines" epic (`MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV`), C6
> documentation roadmap. The epic commits a generated Mermaid flowchart at
> `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd`; this item renders it to a portable
> image so the graph is viewable without a Mermaid-aware renderer and links it
> from the canonical storyline doc.

## Problem statement

The storyline graph is committed only as a Mermaid source file
(`docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd`). Anyone reading the repository on a
plain Markdown viewer, on GitHub without Mermaid support, or in a rendered docs
artefact cannot see the graph and cannot easily tell the shape of the shipped
storylines. Rendering it to a portable SVG in a documented docs step and
linking it from `docs/main-street/storylines.md` makes the graph viewable
everywhere, without requiring a Mermaid-aware renderer.

## Users

- **Content designers / producers** — need to see the storyline shape at a
  glance in the docs, without installing Mermaid tooling.
  - *"As a content designer, I want the storyline graph shown as an image in the
    docs, so I can inspect the shipped chains without a Mermaid renderer."*
- **Developers / reviewers** — need the rendered graph to stay in sync with the
  committed Mermaid source so reviews trust the picture.
  - *"As a reviewer, I want a drift guard between the rendered image and the
    committed `.mmd`, so a stale graph cannot be merged."*
- **Docs build / maintainers** — need a deterministic, reproducible render step
  with no manual copy-paste.
  - *"As a maintainer, I want one documented command that regenerates the
    rendered graph, so the artefact is reproducible."*

## Acceptance Criteria

> **Finalised** per producer answers to Q1–Q3 (2026-10-07): minimal npm render
> step (A); reuse Playwright + `mermaid` devDependency (B); SVG-vs-`.mmd` drift
> guard (A).

1. **Rendered artefact** — a rendered graph image (`docs/main-street/storyline-graph.svg`)
   is committed under `docs/main-street/` and is viewable without a
   Mermaid-aware renderer (SVG preferred; PNG only if SVG cannot be emitted).
2. **Reproducible render step** — a documented npm script renders the committed
   `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd` into the committed image
   deterministically (no RNG, timestamp or wall-clock input; byte-identical on
   re-run). The renderer is a **devDependency only** and does not enter the
   game bundle.
3. **Doc link** — `docs/main-street/storylines.md` embeds or links the rendered
   image (in §7.2 "The shipped graph" and/or §11 "Related documents"),
   documenting the new regeneration command in the §5 tooling table.
4. **Drift guard (validation)** — an automated test/check fails when the
   committed rendered SVG drifts from the committed `.mmd`. The existing
   `.mmd`-vs-`src/card-data.csv` `--check` guard must continue to pass.
5. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No mandatory new runtime dependency for the game** — any renderer
  dependency is a **devDependency** only and must not enter the game bundle.
  Reuse the already-installed `playwright` Chromium (no second Chromium
  download).
- **Determinism** — the render must be reproducible from the committed `.mmd`;
  no timestamps/ids embedded in the output that would churn on every run.
- **Mermaid is the source of truth** — the `.mmd` remains the generated
  artefact of record; the image is derived, never hand-edited.
- **Licensing** — any added dependency must be permissively licensed (MIT,
  Apache-2.0, CC0). The `mermaid` package is MIT.
- **Scope** — do not redesign the graph content or the storyline model, and do
  not build a full static docs site (deferred to `MS-0MUYK064P0032374`). This
  item only renders and links the existing graph.

## Existing state (repo research)

- `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd` — committed 98-line Mermaid flowchart;
  choice cards as diamonds, plain incidents as rounded rectangles, cycle edges
  as `==>`.
- `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` — generator/CLI: `--format mermaid|json`,
  `--out`, `--check` (drift guard). Deterministic (sorted ids, no RNG/clock).
- `src/scripts/storyline-graph-cli.ts` — CLI entry; npm script
  `storylines:graph` (`vite-node src/scripts/storyline-graph-cli.ts`).
- `tests/main-street/storyline-graph.test.ts` — asserts the committed `.mmd`
  matches regeneration from `src/card-data.csv` (existing drift guard).
- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` — canonical doc. §5 Tooling, §7.2 shipped
  graph, §10 Roadmap (links this work item), §11 Related documents (links the
  `.mmd`).
- `package.json` — scripts include `storylines:graph`, `validate:storylines`;
  devDependencies already include `playwright`, `sharp`, `vite-node`/`vite`,
  `vitest`. **No `mermaid`, `@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli`, `puppeteer` or docs site
  generator (mkdocs/docusaurus) is present anywhere in the repo or `core/`.**
- **There is no "docs build"** in `tce-main-street`: `docs/` is plain Markdown,
  there is no docs npm script, no mkdocs/docusaurus config, and no docs-site CI
  workflow. The only Pages workflow (`core/.github/workflows/deploy.yml`)
  deploys the game bundle, not these docs.

## Desired change

1. **Render** the committed `.mmd` into a portable SVG via a documented,
   deterministic script/npm command that reuses the installed Playwright
   Chromium and the `mermaid` JS package (devDependency).
2. **Commit** the rendered SVG under `docs/main-street/`.
3. **Link/embed** the rendered SVG from `docs/main-street/storylines.md` and
   update the §5 tooling table and §10 roadmap row.
4. **Guard** the rendered SVG against drift from the `.mmd` with a test/check;
   document the regeneration workflow.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.svg` — **new** rendered artefact.
- `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd` — input (unchanged source of truth).
- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` — add image embed/link; update §5 tooling,
  §7.2 shipped graph, §10 roadmap.
- `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` — possibly extend with an `svg`/render
  format or a separate renderer module.
- `src/scripts/render-storyline-graph.ts` — **new** render script (if separate
  from the existing CLI).
- `package.json` — new npm script (e.g. `storylines:graph:svg`) and the
  `mermaid` devDependency.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-graph.test.ts` (or a new test) — rendered-image
  drift guard.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV** — "write storylines" epic (completed/in review); this
  item is roadmap item C6-deferred.
- **MS-0MUMP94S7008KTI0** — "Storyline graph/manifest export & JSON schema"
  (completed) — produced `storyline-graph.mmd`, the JSON manifest, and the
  existing `.mmd` drift test this item builds on.
- **MS-0MUMP968H005MXZY** — "Canonical docs, cross-references & doc-drift
  guard" (completed) — owns `docs/main-street/storylines.md` §10 Roadmap and §11
  Related documents.
- **MS-0MUYK064P0032374** — **new**: "Static docs site that renders Mermaid docs
  at build time" (medium, discovered-from this item) — the deferred option (B)
  from Q1.
- **MS-0MUNC8AOL0092BE5** — "Fix stale example-games/main-street paths in docs
  after the src/ migration" (open) — touches the same docs tree; coordinate if
  both touch `storylines.md`.
- **MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9** / **MS-0MUNB5D7K001GH19** — sibling deferred
  storyline roadmap items (conditional options; visual authoring editor).
- **MS-0MUSY1M1F003IS47** — "Editor host & read-only graph viewer" (blocked) —
  the viewer may consume the rendered graph.

### Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0** – Some staff cards should add action points (completed)
- **MS-0MUSY1M1F003IS47** – Editor host & read-only graph viewer (blocked)
- **MS-0MUMP93DI0018OGV** – Storyline model & extraction seam (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: add, already, aware, build, card (+30 more)
- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` — matched: add, already, build, card, check (+28 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: add, already, aware, build, card (+24 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **No docs build exists (MEDIUM).** The premise "in the docs build" has no
  counterpart in the repo. *Mitigation:* Q1 answer (A) creates a minimal render
  step; the full docs-site build is deferred to `MS-0MUYK064P0032374`.
- **Determinism / review churn (MEDIUM).** SVG output can embed ids/timestamps.
  *Mitigation:* assert byte-stable output in a test; pin the `mermaid` version.
- **Headless renderer flakiness in CI (MEDIUM).** Playwright Chromium must be
  available in the test environment. *Mitigation:* reuse the already-installed
  Playwright; keep the render a dev-only npm script and guard it in tests.
- **Drift staleness (LOW).** A committed image can silently diverge from the
  `.mmd`. *Mitigation:* AC4 SVG-vs-`.mmd` drift guard.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Requests to redesign the graph layout, add legends, or
  build a full docs site must be recorded as separate work items, not absorbed
  here (the docs-site request is already tracked as `MS-0MUYK064P0032374`).
- **Assumption** — SVG is the preferred format (scalable, text-searchable);
  PNG is acceptable only if the chosen renderer cannot emit SVG.
- **Assumption** — the `.mmd` stays the generated source of truth; the image is
  derived.
- **Assumption** — CHANGELOG is managed by the release pipeline and is out of
  scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

> **Status: answered.** Producer answers received 2026-10-07 (this session).
> Recommendations were advisory; the producer's choices are recorded below.

- **Q1 — Delivery surface ("the docs build").** *There is no docs build in
  `tce-main-street` (docs are plain Markdown; no mkdocs/docusaurus/Pages
  pipeline). How should the rendered graph be delivered?*
  Options:
  - **(A) Add a minimal render step** — a new npm script that renders
    `storyline-graph.mmd` → `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.svg`, with the SVG
    committed and regenerated like the `.mmd`.
  - **(B) Create a full static docs build** (mkdocs/docusaurus/Pages) that
    renders Mermaid at build time — larger scope, new toolchain.
  - **(C) Commit a one-off rendered SVG** with no build/pipeline; document
    manual regeneration only.
  - **Recommended: (A)** — smallest change that makes the graph viewable
    everywhere and keeps it reproducible, without adopting a docs-site
    toolchain the repo does not otherwise use.
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-07): (A)** — minimal npm render step.
    **Follow-up:** option (B) tracked separately as
    `MS-0MUYK064P0032374` (medium priority). Source: interactive reply.

- **Q2 — Renderer / dependency policy.** *Rendering Mermaid requires a renderer;
  none is installed, and the epic constrained new runtime deps. Which renderer?*
  Options:
  - **(A) Add `@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli` (`mmdc`) as a devDependency** —
    bundles a Puppeteer/Chromium download; heaviest.
  - **(B) Reuse the already-installed `playwright` Chromium** and add the
    `mermaid` JS package as a devDependency, rendering headlessly.
  - **(C) No build-time renderer** — author/commit the SVG manually; guard
    drift only lightly.
  - **Recommended: (B)** — Playwright is already a devDependency (no second
    Chromium download) and keeps the renderer dev-only; the `mermaid` package
    is permissively licensed (MIT).
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-07): (B)** — reuse the already-installed
    Playwright Chromium and add the `mermaid` JS package as a devDependency
    (headless render). Source: interactive reply.

- **Q3 — Drift gate scope.** *Should the new step also fail when the rendered
  SVG drifts from the `.mmd`?*
  Options:
  - **(A) Yes** — add an SVG-vs-`.mmd` drift guard (test/script), in addition
    to the existing `.mmd`-vs-CSV guard.
  - **(B) No** — render the SVG but do not gate on it.
  - **Recommended: (A)** — a stale rendered graph is exactly the failure this
    item is meant to prevent.
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-07): (A)** — add an SVG-vs-`.mmd` drift guard
    on top of the existing `.mmd`-vs-CSV guard. Source: interactive reply.

---

## Reopened scope: per-storyline rendering (2026-10-08)

> **Producer review.** The combined SVG is unreadable: 71 nodes but only 11
> connected (the 5 storyline chains). Mermaid lays the 60 isolated
> (non-storyline) incidents out in a single horizontal row, producing a
> 13,268px-wide strip of tiny boxes. The producer asked to break the graph into
> pages, one parent box per page, with the standalone incidents shown as a
> compact index/table (option C). This is a **rendering/layout change only** —
> the storyline model and the committed `.mmd` source of truth are unchanged.

### Added Acceptance Criteria

7. **Per-storyline pages** — the render step emits one SVG per storyline parent
   (five: tax, health, economy, labor, restaurant), each showing only that
   storyline's chain at a readable size, committed under `docs/main-street/`.
   *Metric: five committed `storyline-graph-<slug>.svg` files; each renders the
   storyline's node/edge subset.*
8. **Standalone-incident index** — the 60 non-storyline incidents are
   represented as a compact index/table (not boxes) and are drift-guarded
   against the manifest. *Metric: index present in `storylines.md` and a test
   regenerates/comparses it from the manifest.*
9. **Docs, guards and tests updated** — `storylines.md` §7.2 embeds the
   per-storyline gallery and the index table; the render `--check` guard and
   the render tests cover every page; the existing `.mmd`-vs-CSV guard stays
   green; the full suite passes. *Metric: full suite green; `--check` exits 0.*

### Design decisions (assumptions recorded)

- One page = one **storyline** (the parent/root incident and its chain), not one
  page per choice card. This keeps the tax cycle (3 cards) together.
- "Compact index/table" is implemented as a generated Markdown table in the
  canonical doc (the natural index for plain Markdown docs), not as boxes.
- The combined `storyline-graph.mmd` remains the generated source of truth; the
  monolithic combined SVG is replaced by the per-storyline pages.

---

## Reopened scope: per-event detail tables (2026-10-08)

> **Producer review.** The per-storyline diagrams show only the event names.
> The producer asked for much more information about each event in a storyline:
> the descriptive text, the impact on game state, and anything else critical.
> Presentation chosen: a **detail table below each diagram** (option A).

### Added Acceptance Criteria

10. **Event detail data** — the storyline manifest exposes, for every event,
    its descriptive text (`effect`), `trigger`, `tier`, `cost`,
    `target`/`targetSynergy`, `coinDelta`/`reputationDelta`/`coinPercentDelta`,
    `duration`/`effectType`/`multiplier`, and the per-option `effectPolicy`;
    the JSON schema is extended and the schema drift test stays green.
    *Metric: manifest node/edge fields present; schema validation passes.*
11. **Per-event detail tables** — a generated detail table (one row per event:
    description, normalised game-state impact, choice routing) is rendered below
    each per-storyline diagram in `storylines.md` §7.2. *Metric: tables present
    and readable.*
12. **Drift guard + docs + full suite** — the detail tables are drift-guarded
    against the manifest (`npm run storylines:graph:svg -- --check` and a test);
    the docs are updated; the full suite passes. *Metric: `--check` exits 0;
    full suite green.*

### Design decisions (assumptions recorded)

- The tables are generated between `<!-- BEGIN/END GENERATED -->` markers in
  `storylines.md`; the render step splices only the marked regions, so hand-
  written prose is never clobbered.
- Table rows lead with the event **name** (with the id) and use four columns so
  they do not collide with the §7.2 chains-table parser in the doc-drift test.
- `tier` comes from the exported `CARD_TIER_MAP`; duration fields are read from
  the `DurationEventCard` variant.

---

## Reopened scope: per-storyline docs, assets folder, richer boxes (2026-10-08)

> **Producer review.** The detail tables added the information but the doc is
> still not readable: `storylines.md` is now long, and the diagram boxes show
> only the name/id. Producer requirements: separate each storyline's `.md` from
> `storylines.md`; move the SVGs into an assets folder; and put a brief
> description + game-state impact inside each box.

### Added Acceptance Criteria

13. **Per-storyline documents** — each storyline has its own committed Markdown
    document (`docs/main-street/storylines/<slug>.md`) containing its diagram
    and per-event detail table; `storylines.md` links to them and no longer
    embeds the diagrams/tables. *Metric: 5 per-storyline docs; `storylines.md`
    contains links, not embeds.*
14. **Assets folder** — the rendered SVGs live under
    `docs/main-street/assets/` (`storyline-graph-<slug>.svg`) and every
    reference (docs, tests, guards) uses the new path. *Metric: no committed
    SVG remains at the old path; links resolve.*
15. **Readable boxes** — each diagram box shows a brief form of the event's
    description and its game-state impact (not just name/id). *Metric: rendered
    SVG node labels contain the brief text and impact; drift guard updated.*

### Design decisions (assumptions recorded)

- "Brief form of the description" = the first sentence of the card's `effect`
  text, truncated to a bounded length.
- "Game-state impact" = the normalised impact already computed for the detail
  tables (coin/reputation deltas, proportional coin loss, duration multiplier).
- Assets live at `docs/main-street/assets/` (no existing docs-asset convention;
  `screenshots/` is unrelated and specific to screenshots).
- The per-storyline docs are generated (like the incident index) and
  drift-guarded, so the tables/diagrams never drift from the manifest.

---

## Reopened scope: actionable drift-test failures (2026-10-08)

> **Producer review.** When a drift guard fails it names the stale artefact but
> does not say how to fix it. The failure output must include the command(s) to
> regenerate the committed docs.

### Added Acceptance Criteria

16. **Actionable test failures** — every storyline-docs drift assertion emits
    the exact regeneration command(s) in its failure output (Vitest custom
    message), so a developer can fix a stale artefact without reading the
    source. *Metric: failing assertion output contains
    `npm run storylines:graph:svg` (and the `.mmd`/JSON commands where
    relevant).*

### Design decisions (assumptions recorded)

- Use Vitest's `expect(actual, message)` custom message so the hint precedes the
  value diff.
- One shared hint constant per test file, tailored to the artefacts it guards:
  - SVG/doc drift → `npm run storylines:graph:svg`
  - `.mmd`/manifest drift → `npm run storylines:graph -- --format mermaid|json`

# Implement free market re-roll mechanic (engine + state + bias draw)

**Summary:** Add the engine logic for the Investor's free market re-roll: per-turn state tracking, the bias-aware draw algorithm, and the integration with the existing market refill path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- While at least one Investor is employed, the player may perform one coin-free, action-free market re-roll per week/turn (no coin deduction, no action spent); multiple Investors do not stack (still one per turn). The free re-roll is gated by a per-turn flag reset at `WeekStart` alongside `peekUsedThisTurn`/`favourUsedThisTurn`, and it advances the per-turn escalation counter (`marketRefreshesThisTurn`, MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ) so the next paid re-roll costs the escalated price. Once used, further re-rolls fall back to the normal paid path.
- On the Investor's free re-roll, each drawn slot has a 75% chance to be drawn from the "relevant" pool for the business the Investor is employed at, falling back to the fully random pool when the relevant pool is exhausted; the remaining probability is entirely random. Relevance is defined as a shared synergy type (business/community-space synergyTypes; event targetSynergy/effect; staff allowedBusinessTypes overlap with the hosting business's synergy types).
- The biased draw uses the seeded RNG (`state.rng`) so same-seed produces same-game determinism.
- `refillSingleRowMarket` is parameterised to accept the bias/relevance pool; the normal `refreshMarket`/`cycleMarketCards` paths stay fully random.
- The bias draw preserves the >=1-business row composition invariant.

**Parent Coverage:** Implements parent AC2 (One free re-roll per turn) and parent AC3 (Relevance bias).

**Minimal Implementation:**
- Add `investorFreeRerollUsedThisTurn` to state types
- Reset flag at `WeekStart`
- Implement `canUseFreeMarketReroll` / `useFreeMarketReroll`
- Implement bias-aware draw in `refillSingleRowMarket`
- Wire up the bias detection (hosting business synergy types overlap)

**Dependencies:** Add Investor card to catalog (CSV + types + parsing)

**Deliverables:** Engine functions, state field, bias draw algorithm, WeekStart reset.

**Key Files:**
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`
- `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts`
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts`
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` or `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts`

# Intake Brief: Re-evaluate Upgrade Costs/ROI After the Five-Turn Payback Rebalance

**Work item:** MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M · `task` · `high`
**Discovered from:** MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3 (Game balance: business payback to ~5 turns)
**Recommendation R1:** Re-evaluate upgrade costs/incomeBonus so upgrades clear the ~5-turn payback opportunity cost.

## Headline

The five-turn payback rebalance (MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3) left upgrades severely under-valued: 9 of 39 upgrade cards show 0% adoption on the after-state, and the expensive tier (cost 7–14) is universally rejected by the greedy AI. This task re-derives upgrade `cost` and `incomeBonus` values so upgrades are genuinely worth purchasing in a meaningful share of runs.

## Problem statement

Businesses now recover their cost in ~5 turns, making each turn of play more economically tense. However, an upgrade must (a) require a parent business to already be owned, and (b) spend 3–14 coins on top of the business's remaining payback, so upgrades rarely clear the opportunity cost before the run ends. With `incomeBonus` values set proportionally to upgrade cost (e.g. cost 9 → bonus 300), the ROI `incomeBonus × horizon − cost` is positive only when `horizon` is large — but runs last ~10–12 turns on average, and the AI's planning horizon (floor=5, cap=25) means cheap upgrades barely clear positive-NPV. The expensive tier never does.

## Users

- **Player** — wants building decisions to carry real economic tension, including meaningful upgrade choices (e.g. "Should I invest in my Diner or bank these coins?"). Currently, upgrades feel like dead ends.
- **Producer / designer** — wants a diverse economy where investment (upgrades) is a viable strategy alongside banking and business expansion.
- **Developer** — wants the changes to be small, targeted, and reversible, backed by before/after Monte Carlo evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Baseline captured.** The current upgrade pick rate (M1: purchases / market appearances) and M5 adoption (upgrade purchases / parent purchases) are recorded from the after-state canonical profile (200 seeds, 60 max turns, `mc-balance`, greedy). Results documented in the work-item description.
2. **Changes applied.** Upgrade `cost` and/or `incomeBonus` values in `src/card-data.csv` are adjusted so that at least the cheap upgrades (cost ≤5) reach a measurable pick rate and the expensive tier reaches a non-trivial pick rate. **No engine-rule changes.**
3. **Before/after evidence.** The canonical Monte Carlo profile is re-run post-change; pick rates and adoption rates are recorded as a before/after comparison. Win-rate ladder Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard is preserved.
4. **Full test suite passes** with the new values (`npm test`).

> Standard criteria also met: at least one testing/validation criterion (AC2), documentation updated where relevant, and full suite green (AC4). CHANGELOG.md is excluded (managed by the ship pipeline); no CI/CD pipeline tests.

## Constraints

- **No engine-rule changes** (card-data.csv is the only lever).
- **Integer ×100 economy** — costs and bonuses are integer coin-cent units.
- **Preserve the win-rate ladder** (Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard) as the primary gate.
- **Scope-creep guard:** Community-space pricing, event pricing, and business income are out of scope; record as linked follow-ups.
- **Budget discipline:** Changes must not materially shift win rates (±0.05 on Medium) — upgrades represent a small share of total income.

## Existing state

### Post-rebalance after-state (commit 8b8fe46, current dev tip — card-data unchanged since rebalance)

**200 seeds / 60 turns / Medium / greedy Monte Carlo (canonical profile):**

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Runs with ≥1 upgrade | 31.0% (62/200) |
| Aggregate M1 pick rate (all upgrades) | 8.18% (88/1076 appearances) |
| Upgrade share of all purchases | 8.43% (89/1056) |
| Aggregate M5 adoption (upgrade vs parent owns) | ~10.50% |

### Upgrade performance (after-state, sorted by M1 pick rate)

**Top performers (M1 ≥ 15%):**
| Upgrade | Cost | incomeBonus | M1 Pick Rate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| upg-gourmet-truck | 3 | 150 | 24.0% |
| upg-gaming-lounge | 7 | 200 | 23.8% |
| upg-gourmet-deli | 4 | 150 | 19.2% |
| upg-bistro | 3 | 100 | 18.8% |
| upg-bespoke-tailor | 4 | 100 | 17.9% |

**Mid performers (M1 5–15%):**
upg-readers-cafe (17.4%), upg-patisserie (16.7%), upg-roastery (12.1%), upg-wellness-retreat (12.1%), upg-tea-lounge (12.0%), upg-resort-spa (11.5%), upg-smoothie-bar (11.5%), upg-grand-fountain (11.1%), upg-adventure-park (10.3%), upg-community-hub (9.4%), upg-vintage-shop (9.1%), upg-garden (8.7%), upg-orchard (8.7%)

**Low performers (M1 0–5%):**
upg-designer-store (7.7%), upg-fast-food (7.4%), upg-drive-in (7.1%), upg-fitness-center (6.7%), upg-garden-center (6.5%), upg-bread-factory (6.5%), upg-toy-warehouse (6.5%), upg-dry-cleaners (5.7%), upg-imax (4.8%), upg-health-center (3.7%), upg-wellness-center (3.2%), upg-private-medical-center (3.1%)

**Never picked (M1 = 0%):**
upg-home-improvement, upg-salon, upg-museum, upg-medical-center, upg-grand-bakehouse, upg-restaurant, upg-multiplex, upg-luxury-retreat, upg-dental-clinic (9 upgrades)

### AI upgrade scoring formula

```
score = incomeBonus × horizon − cost
horizon = clamp(ceil((winThreshold - score) / scorePace), 5, 25)
```

For a 0-turn-horizon floor of 5:
- Cost 3, bonus 100 → score = 500 − 300 = **+200** (positive, competitive)
- Cost 9, bonus 300 → score = 1500 − 900 = **+600** (positive at floor, but expensive)
- Cost 14, bonus 550 → score = 2750 − 1400 = **+1350** (positive but very high cost)

The expensive upgrades' high `incomeBonus` values make them look attractive on paper, but their high `cost` means they rarely appear in the market before the game ends, and when they do, the AI prioritises cheaper alternatives with better cost-adjusted returns.

## Desired change

1. **Raise `incomeBonus` or lower `cost` for the 0%-tier upgrades.** Target: lift the top cheap upgrades to ≥20% M1 pick rate and the expensive tier to ≥5% M1 pick rate.
2. **Adjust the cheap tier upward modestly** if they fall below the target.
3. **Document every change with rationale.**
4. **Re-run Monte Carlo and compare.**

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — Upgrade row edits (`cost`, `incomeBonus`).
- `tests/main-street/business-payback.test.ts` — May need update if cost/income changes affect business payback (unlikely, as upgrades are a separate family).
- `src/scripts/balance/engine/card-metrics.ts` — M5 `computeUpgradeAdoption` may need base-ID normalisation (instance-suffixed `cardsOwned` vs. base card IDs).
- `docs/main-street/` — Update balance documentation with before/after results.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3** — Game balance: business payback to ~5 turns (parent context).
- **MS-0MUQUBJQF009PTZ0** — Re-tune compensating balance levers (deferred upgrade pricing to this item).
- **MS-0MUQUBKNE007NYR8** — Further-balancing recommendations (R1: upgrade re-pricing).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Premise nuance (research finding).** The "≤1% of runs" claim in the further-balancing report appears to refer to per-upgrade individual run-participation (many are ≤1%). However, the aggregate picture is more nuanced: 31% of runs pick ≥1 upgrade, and the cheap tier already shows 16–24% M1 pick rates. Only the expensive tier (cost 7–9+) is truly broken at 0%. This may narrow the scope.
- **Metric definition note.** The M1/M5 functions (`computePickRate`, `computeUpgradeAdoption`) compare base card IDs against instance-suffixed `cardsOwned` entries (e.g., `biz-laundromat-1`). The baseline should either (a) normalise IDs by stripping `-N` suffixes or (b) use instance IDs consistently. This is a known pattern in `MainStreetCardsUtils.ts`.
- **No engine-rule changes.** Changes are card-data only; the scoring formula and horizon remain unchanged.
- **Scope-creep risk.** If producer wants community-space or event pricing adjustments too, record as linked follow-ups.
- **Budget discipline.** Upgrade income is a small share of total income, so changes should have minimal impact on overall win rates. The win-rate ladder should be preserved.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (success metric & scope — OPEN QUESTION):** *What is the success threshold, and which upgrade tiers need fixing?*
  - **Recommended: B** — Focus on the expensive tier (cost ≥7) where 9 upgrades hit 0% adoption. Cheap upgrades already perform at 16–24% M1.
  - Option A: Fix all upgrades, target ≥5% M1 for every upgrade.
  - Option B: Fix only expensive tier (cost ≥7), target ≥5% M1.
  - Option C: Accept current cheap-tier performance; only fix expensive tier to ≥10% M1.

  **Answer (producer):** B- **Q2 (change scope — OPEN QUESTION):** *What is in bounds for changes?*
  - **Recommended: A** — `cost` + `incomeBonus` in card-data.csv only.
  - Option A: Cost + incomeBonus only.
  - Option B: Also adjust AI horizon parameters (AI_HORIZON_FLOOR, scoring formula).
  - Option C: Also adjust guardrail preservation requirements.

  **Answer (producer):** A- **Q3 (premise accuracy — OPEN QUESTION):** *The data shows 31% of runs pick ≥1 upgrade (aggregate M1 = 8.18%). The "≤1% of runs" claim in the report refers to per-upgrade individual participation. Should the goal be to lift ALL upgrades above the current floor, or only the broken tier?*
  - **Recommended: B** — The expensive tier (9 upgrades at 0%) is the real problem; cheap upgrades already meet a reasonable baseline.

  **Answer (producer):** B
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0** – Some staff cards should add action points (completed)
- **MS-0MTR39XO6002CBB1** – Events income/costs should be shown on the business cards (open)
- **MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M** – Implement IT Specialist and Delivery Driver cost-reduction effects (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: ac4, accept, acceptance, affect, aggregate (+275 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: accept, acceptance, adjust, adjustments, affect (+251 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md` — matched: 0muq50i1y000b6l3, accept, adoption, affect, aggregate (+241 more)

## Implementation evidence (MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M)

**Change:** expensive-tier upgrade ROI re-evaluation — card data only, **no engine-rule change**.

**Canonical profile:** 200 seeds, seed-prefix `mc-balance`, 60 max turns, greedy, sweep Easy/Medium/Hard. Before = pre-change dev tip; After = this change.

### AC1/AC2 — expensive-tier upgrades lifted off 0%

The four level-0 upgrades whose parent businesses are built infrequently had **0% M1** on the canonical Medium profile because the single upgrade market slot rarely surfaced them while the parent was owned (co-occurrence, not affordability). They were discounted toward their balance-curve cost and given the producer-approved `drawWeight` deck-composition lever (from MS-0MUYK08I1004I19W):

| Upgrade | Target (level 0) | cost before -> after | drawWeight | Medium M1 before -> after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `upg-designer-store` | Boutique | 700 -> **600** | - -> **3** | 0.0% (0/19) -> **14.7% (10/68)** |
| `upg-museum` | Art Gallery | 700 -> **600** | - -> **3** | 0.0% (0/18) -> **8.5% (4/47)** |
| `upg-dental-clinic` | Dentist | 700 -> **600** | - -> **3** | 0.0% (0/23) -> **17.7% (11/62)** |
| `upg-private-medical-center` | Private Clinic | 900 -> **700** | - -> **3** | 0.0% (0/22) -> **16.1% (10/62)** |

All four now clear >=5% M1 on the canonical Medium profile with non-zero absolute purchase counts. `drawWeight` is the operative lever: prior experiments (MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4) showed cost/`incomeBonus` alone cannot move adoption because co-occurrence is the binding constraint. The cost reductions re-derive ROI (AC2 wording); the weights make the cards reachable.

### AC3 — before/after evidence and win-rate ladder

| Difficulty | Win-rate before -> after |
|---|---|
| Easy | 76.5% -> 76.0% |
| Medium | 66.5% -> 66.0% |
| Hard | 41.5% -> 41.5% |

Easy >= Medium >= Hard preserved; Medium moved -0.5 pp (within the +/-5 pp / +/-0.05 band). Medium capstone reachability retained: `upg-grand-bakehouse` 7.5%->11.3%, `upg-restaurant` 8.8%->10.5%, `upg-multiplex` 11.3%->7.7%, `upg-luxury-retreat` 3.6%->2.0% (small-n; ~50 appearances each).

### AC4 — testing

`tests/main-street/upgrade-draw-weight.test.ts` gains an "expensive-tier ROI re-evaluation" block pinning the four re-derived costs/`drawWeight`, the level-0 gate and target business, and the positive-NPV check at the AI horizon floor. `group-e-upgrade-cards-expansion.test.ts` and `clinic-health-synergy.test.ts` contracts updated. Docs (`card-catalog.md`, `balancing-methodology.md`) and the derived card SVGs + `csv-checksum.json` regenerated. Full suite green via the test skill (scope=full, 65 s).

### Scope note

The branching prerequisites `upg-drive-in` (700) and `upg-wellness-center` (900) remain below target on some profiles; they compete with the standard path weighted by MS-0MUYK08I1004I19W. Over-tuning the single-slot upgrade market to lift them regressed the capstone `upg-luxury-retreat`, so they are left as-is and flagged for a separate follow-up rather than risk the approved capstone fix.

# Intake Brief: Re-tune Reputation Sources for the Slower-Coin Economy (Medium Loss Mode)

**Work item:** MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE · `task` · `high`
**Discovered from:** MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3 (Game balance: business payback to ~5 turns)
**Recommendation R2:** [further-balancing-recommendations.md §5](docs/main-street/further-balancing-recommendations.md)

## Headline

After the five-turn payback rebalance (MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3) reduced business
`baseIncome` by ~2.4×, **reputation collapse became the dominant Medium loss
mode — 69% of losses vs. 30% bankruptcy** (was bankruptcy-dominated). The
economy now produces fewer surplus coins to convert into reputation via
Community Favour, while passive business `reputationPerTurn` was left
unchanged. This task re-tunes reputation sources so the Medium loss-mode split
returns to the PRD design-intent band (reputation collapse 20–40% of losses,
bankruptcy 40–70%) while keeping the win-rate ladder `Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard`.

## Problem statement

The five-turn payback rebalance deliberately tightened the economy (producer
decision Q3 = C, MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3), leaving net liquidity slack (2–4
coins/turn) but starving the reputation economy: with base incomes ~2.4× lower,
there are far fewer surplus coins to spend on Community Favour
(`favourCoinsToRepCost` = 200 coins → 1 reputation, unchanged on all presets),
and business/community-space `reputationPerTurn` values are unchanged. On
Medium, 69% of losses are now reputation collapses, against a PRD guardrail of
20–40% of losses ([prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md](docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md)
§G5 / guardrail table). Hard remains balanced at 48/52, which reads as a healthy
challenge spread — the distortion is Medium-specific.

## Users

- **Player** — wants losses to come from a mix of economic and reputational
  pressure, not a single dominant failure mode that makes the town feel
  impossible to keep alive.
  - *"As a player, I want reputation to recover at a pace that matches the
    slower coin economy, so that a run can be lost to bankruptcy or to
    reputation, not only to reputation."*
- **Producer / game designer** — wants the documented loss-mode design intent
  restored and evidenced, with the win-rate ladder preserved.
  - *"As a designer, I want the Medium loss-mode split back inside the PRD
    band, backed by before/after Monte Carlo evidence and a reproducible
    commit SHA."*
- **Developer** — wants a small, reversible, card-data/config-only change with
  deterministic tests and no engine-rule churn.
  - *"As a developer, I want the reputation-source values and the loss-mode
    target asserted by tests so future rebalances cannot silently regress."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Before-state captured.** The after-five-turn-payback baseline is measured
   on the canonical profile (200 seeds, `mc-balance`, 60 max turns, greedy;
   Easy/Medium/Hard) and recorded with its commit SHA: per-difficulty win
   rates and the Medium **loss-only** decomposition (reputation collapse /
   bankruptcy / other). Recorded in the work item.
2. **Evidence-led re-tune applied within the named levers.** Business and
   community-space `reputationPerTurn` and/or `favourCoinsToRepCost` (and, where
   evidenced, community-space reputation pricing) are adjusted in
   `src/card-data.csv` / `src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts`. **No engine-rule
   changes** (score formula, action economy, synergy formula, collapse
   threshold, discard reputation penalty are out of scope). Each changed value
   is justified against the measured loss decomposition.
3. **Target loss-mode mix achieved.** On the canonical profile after the
   changes, the Medium loss-only split meets the PRD band:
   - reputation collapse **20–40% of losses** (G5 target 30–40%);
   - bankruptcy **40–70% of losses** (G5 target 50–60%);
   and the primary balance gate holds: win-rate ladder
   `Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard`, with each difficulty inside its PRD win-rate band
   (Medium 20–85%, Easy 45–95%, Hard 5–60%).
4. **Before/after evidence recorded.** Before → after loss-mode decomposition
   and win rates per difficulty, with commit SHAs, are summarised in the work
   item **and** a `docs/main-street/` artefact. The committed baseline
   (`docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json`) is regenerated **only** via
   the drift-report-then-ask workflow
   ([balance-guardrail-recommendations.md §0](docs/main-street/balance-guardrail-recommendations.md))
   with producer approval — never silently.
5. **Testing / validation.** At least one automated test asserts the tuned
   reputation-source invariants (e.g. the Community Favour rate and the
   reputation-generating card values), and the loss-mode target is captured by
   the balance metric output (G5) so a regression is detectable.
6. **Documentation updated.** All related documentation is updated to reflect
   the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
   site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Engine rules out of scope.** Per the parent's non-recommendations
  (score formula, action economy, synergy formula) — this is a parameter
  re-tune, not a rules change. The reputation-collapse threshold (`rep <= 0`)
  and the discard-cost reputation penalty are engine/rule behaviour and are
  not to be changed here.
- **Difficulty presets are unchanged** (parent decision Q3 = C); the win-rate
  ladder `Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard` is the primary gate.
- **Do not raise `baseIncome`** — the five-turn payback contract
  (net payback 4.5–5.5 turns) must be preserved.
- **No new cards.** Use existing reputation sources only.
- **Evidence first.** Every parameter change must be justified by a measured
  before/after Monte Carlo run; the drift-report-then-ask workflow governs any
  committed-baseline regeneration.

## Existing state

**Reputation sources (current values, `src/card-data.csv` unless noted):**

- **Business `reputationPerTurn`** — 30 of 31 businesses carry it (e.g. Bakery
  +5, Café +10, Gallery/Spa/Private Clinic +25, Hotel +30, Clinic +40 with 0
  base income, Pawn Shop −10). Unchanged by the payback rebalance.
- **Community-space `reputationPerTurn`** — all 8: Park 0, Playground +5,
  Library/Garden/Fountain +10, Health Kiosk/Shelter +15, Public Art +20.
  These are the R4 (MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5) re-pricing candidates.
- **Community Favour** (`src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts`) — all three presets:
  `favourCoinsToRepCost = 200` coins → 1 rep; `favourRepToCoinsRepCost = 200`
  rep → `favourRepToCoinsCoinGain = 300` coins. Free, once per turn.
- **Positive events** — large one-shot `reputationDelta` on many events
  (e.g. `evt-charity-drive` +1350, `evt-volunteer-day` +1400, seasonal
  `evt-christmas` +650); negative events −100 each.
- **Storylines / upgrades** — `reputationBonus` on upgrade cards, storyline
  effects.

**Loss mechanic.** Reputation collapse fires when `resourceBank.reputation <= 0`
after turn 1 (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`). Loss-mode decomposition is
computed in `src/scripts/balance/engine/global-metrics.ts` (G5) as
`lossesByMode[l] / totalLosses`.

**Design-intent bands (PRD §G5 / guardrail table):** bankruptcy 40–70% of
losses (target 50–60%); reputation collapse 20–40% of losses (target 30–40%);
timeout < 15%. Medium greedy win rate 20–85%.

**Current after-state (commit `8b8fe46`, [payback-rebalance-evidence.md](docs/main-street/payback-rebalance-evidence.md)):**
Medium win rate 0.325; loss-only split reputation collapse **69%** /
bankruptcy **30%** / other 1%. Hard 48/52.

**Greedy-AI caveat.** The greedy strategy scores `community-favour`
(`coins-to-rep`) at score **1** and treats it as a fallback that never
outranks a purchase (`src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` ~L1379). Changing
`favourCoinsToRepCost` alone may therefore not move greedy behaviour unless the
AI is stalled; passive `reputationPerTurn` is likely the primary lever.

## Desired change

Restore the Medium loss-mode split to the PRD band by re-tuning reputation
sources so reputation recovery keeps pace with the slower coin economy — a
card-data / config change, evidence-led and reversible, that preserves the
win-rate ladder and the five-turn payback contract.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — reputation source values: business / community-space
  `reputationPerTurn`, event `reputationDelta`, upgrade `reputationBonus`.
- `src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts` — `favourCoinsToRepCost` /
  `favourRepToCoins*` per preset (if Community Favour is tuned).
- `src/scripts/generate-card-csv.ts` — CSV pipeline (if values are regenerated
  from templates).
- `src/scripts/balance/engine/global-metrics.ts` — loss-mode decomposition (G5).
- `src/scripts/balance/guards/thresholds.ts` — `reputationCollapseRate_greedy_medium`
  band (currently defined but not enforced on the simulation).
- `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-greedy-guardrail.test.ts` — design-intent
  win-rate bands.
- `tests/main-street/balance/` — balance metric tests.
- `docs/main-street/` — new before/after evidence artefact.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — coins-to-rep heuristic (out of scope unless a
  producer-approved scope decision is needed to make a lever effective).

## Related work

- **MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3** — parent: five-turn payback rebalance and economy
  re-tune (in-progress). Source of the Q3 = C decision and constraint set.
- **MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M** — R1: re-evaluate upgrade costs/ROI (sibling).
- **MS-0MUR9IMXE0090WIV** — R3: confirm win thresholds / run length as the
  difficulty lever (sibling; interacts with loss mix).
- **MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5** — R4: re-price community spaces / events relative to
  slower business payback (sibling; **overlaps** community-space reputation
  pricing — coordinate to avoid conflicting edits).
- **MS-0MUR9INHX001QCSE** — R5: track synergy diversity (G4/HHI) post-rebalance.
- **MS-0MUAYBAHW007RMSL** — Add a charity shop (reputation-leaning Culture card;
  `reputationPerTurn = 15`, producer-set cost override).
- **MS-0MURC6XO8005W57D** — Closing a business damages reputation (interacts
  with reputation pressure).
- **MS-0MTV9AS15004AC1E** — Visual representation of reputation (UI, out of scope).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — win-rate lift.** Reducing reputation-collapse losses raises the
  Medium win rate. The PRD band is wide (20–85%) and the ladder is the gate,
  but any move beyond the committed-baseline drift tolerance requires the
  drift-report-then-ask workflow and producer sign-off.
- **Risk — lever effectiveness.** The greedy AI scores coins-to-rep at 1, so
  `favourCoinsToRepCost` tuning alone may not change AI behaviour; the passive
  `reputationPerTurn` lever is likely decisive. If an AI-heuristic change is
  required, treat it as an explicit scope decision, not a silent edit.
- **Risk — overlap with R4.** Community-space/event re-pricing (R4) touches the
  same cards; sequence or coordinate to avoid conflicting edits.
- **Risk — overlap with R3.** Win thresholds / run length (R3) also shift the
  loss mix; changing both at once confounds attribution — land R2 first or
  measure independently.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Keep the change to reputation sources; do not
  rebalance upgrades, broad event economies, or add cards (record extra
  opportunities as linked work items).
- **Assumption.** The PRD loss-mode bands are authoritative; the target is
  reputation collapse 20–40% of Medium losses (G5 30–40%), bankruptcy
  40–70% (G5 50–60%).
- **Assumption.** Canonical profile = 200 seeds, prefix `mc-balance`, 60 max
  turns, greedy strategy, Easy/Medium/Hard.
- **Assumption.** Card-data / config parameters are in scope; engine rules are
  not (per parent constraints).
- **Assumption.** The committed baseline is only regenerated via
  drift-report-then-ask with producer approval.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No producer questions were required — the design intent is documented in-repo.
The following were resolved by research (recorded for auditability):

- Q: What is a "healthy loss-mode mix"? — Answer (research): the PRD

  `docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md` L138–139, L507–514.
- Q: Which reputation sources are in scope? — Answer (research): the work-item
  AC names business `reputationPerTurn`, Community Favour
  (`favourCoinsToRepCost`), and community-space reputation cards; the parent's
  non-recommendations exclude engine-rule changes. Source: work-item
  description; `docs/main-street/further-balancing-recommendations.md` §6.
- Q: Is preserving the exact win rate required? — Answer (research): no — the
  primary gate is the ladder `Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard`; the PRD win-rate bands
  (Medium 20–85%) and the drift-report-then-ask workflow govern acceptable
  movement. Source: `docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md`
  guardrail table; `docs/main-street/balance-guardrail-recommendations.md` §0.

# Intake Brief: Greedy AI should spend less reputation on Community Favour

**Work item:** MS-0MUVB2ZES005V83Y · `bug` · `high`
**Discovered from:** observed greedy-AI behaviour on the post-payback-rebalance economy
**Related recommendation:** [further-balancing-recommendations.md §5 R2](docs/main-street/further-balancing-recommendations.md) / MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE (reputation re-tune)

## Headline

The greedy AI converts reputation into coins via Community Favour (`rep→coins`)
roughly **2–3.5 times per run** and **never** converts coins into reputation
(`coins→rep`), bleeding the reputation buffer that its own loss condition
(`reputation <= 0`) depends on. It should only exchange when the coins **enable
a profitable placement** and the timing/synergy value of that placement
justifies the reputation spent.

## Problem statement

Community Favour (`CG-0MSTOATDQ005XDET`) is a free, once-per-turn exchange. The
greedy AI takes the `rep→coins` direction (200 reputation → 300 coins) whenever
its turn is *stalled* (it cannot afford the cheapest market card) and it holds a
single-reputation buffer — `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`
(`scoreAction` → `case 'community-favour'`, and the competitive mirror
`competitiveFavourScore`). The check tests neither whether the gained coins
**buy anything profitable** nor whether the resulting placement carries enough
synergy/timing value to justify the reputation cost. Because reputation collapse
(`reputation <= 0` after turn 1) is a loss condition, the fallback trades a
loss-causing resource for liquidity the AI cannot turn into a win.

## Users

- **Player (single-player)** — wants an AI opponent/baseline that plays the
  economy sensibly and does not self-destruct by over-trading reputation for
  coins.
  - *"As a player, I want the greedy AI to look after its reputation, so that
    losses come from the economy, not from the AI repeatedly selling its
    reputation for coins it cannot use well."*
- **Producer / game designer** — wants documented, measurable AI decision
  quality so balance conclusions drawn from greedy simulations remain valid.
  - *"As a designer, I want the greedy AI to use Community Favour only when it
    enables a profitable, well-synergised placement, backed by before/after
    evidence."*
- **Developer** — wants a small, well-tested heuristic change with deterministic
  unit tests, no engine-rule churn, and preserved balance guardrails.
  - *"As a developer, I want the favour heuristic and its guard rails pinned by
    tests so a future balance change cannot silently re-introduce the bleed."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Baseline captured.** The current greedy behaviour is measured on the
   canonical profile (200 seeds, prefix `mc-balance`, 60 max turns, greedy, all
   three difficulties) and recorded in the work item with its commit SHA:
   `rep→coins` uses per run, `coins→rep` uses per run, the reputation-collapse
   share of losses, and per-difficulty win rates. (Indicative 60-seed sample
   from intake research: `rep→coins` 3.52 / 3.12 / 2.18 uses per run on
   Easy/Medium/Hard; `coins→rep` 0; Medium reputation-collapse 29/39 losses ≈
   74%.)
2. **Enablement test added.** The `rep→coins` decision only fires when the
   coins gained (`favourRepToCoinsCoinGain`) actually **enable affording at
   least one card whose greedy placement value (`scoreBusinessAction` /
   `scorePlayBusinessFromHandAction`, i.e. income + synergy over
   `aiPlanningHorizon`) is **positive after** the exchange. A stalled turn that
   would still be unable to afford a profitable card must **not** exchange.
3. **Value/timing gate added.** Among exchanges that pass AC2, the decision
   requires the enabled placement's reward (income + projected synergy over the
   remaining planning horizon) to clear a **named, documented threshold**
   relative to the reputation spent — so that only *early, high-value*
   placements (e.g. securing a strong synergy slot) justify the exchange. The
   threshold is a constant in `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` and must be justified
   with the AC1/AC5 evidence.
4. **Reputation buffer preserved or strengthened.** The existing guard
   (reputation after the exchange stays `>= 1`) is retained; any strengthening
   (e.g. a larger post-exchange buffer) is explicit and tested.
5. **Before/after behaviour recorded.** On the canonical profile after the
   change, per-difficulty `rep→coins` uses per run are **materially lower** than
   the AC1 baseline and the Medium reputation-collapse share of losses **does
   not increase**, while the primary balance gate holds: the win-rate ladder
   `Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard` and the committed-baseline tolerances (`winRate
   ±0.25`, `coins ±30%`; [monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts](tests/main-street/monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts)).
   Before/after figures and commit SHAs are recorded in the work item and a
   `docs/main-street/` artefact. If any committed-baseline drift beyond
   tolerance is required, follow the drift-report-then-ask workflow — never
   regenerate the baseline silently.
6. **Testing / validation.** Automated tests in
   `tests/main-street/community-favour-ai.test.ts` (extended) or a dedicated
   test file pin the new decision: exchange **declined** when it would not
   enable a profitable placement; exchange **declined** when the enabled
   placement is not early/high-value; exchange **taken** when it enables a
   high-value early synergy placement; the reputation-buffer guard; and
   deterministic selection. Existing Community Favour AI tests are updated to
   the new contract rather than deleted.
7. **Documentation updated.** All related documentation is updated to reflect
   the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
   site entries (in particular `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md` and the
   Community Favour move-evaluation notes).
8. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **No engine-rule changes** — Community Favour costs/gains
  (`favourCoinsToRepCost`, `favourRepToCoinsRepCost`,
  `favourRepToCoinsCoinGain`), the action economy, the score formula, the synergy
  formula, and the `reputation <= 0` collapse threshold are **out of scope**.
  This is a heuristic change only (confirmed by intake research measuring that
  parameter-only tuning did not move greedy behaviour — MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE).
- **No card-data rebalance.** Reputation sources/Pricing are owned by R2
  (MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE) and R4 (MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5); do not change
  `src/card-data.csv` here.
- **Preserve determinism.** Same seed + same state → same decision.
- **Preserve the win-rate ladder.** The primary balance gate is
  `Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard`; the change must not invert it.
- **Evidence first.** Every threshold introduced must be justified against the
  measured before/after behaviour; the committed baseline is regenerated only
  via the drift-report-then-ask workflow with producer approval.

## Existing state

**Decision site.** `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`:

- `scoreAction` → `case 'community-favour'` (~L1363): `coins→rep` always scores
  `1`; `rep→coins` scores `3` when
  `coins < getCheapestMarketCost(state)` **and**
  `reputation >= favourRepToCoinsRepCost + 1`, otherwise `1`.
- `chooseGreedyAction` Priority 9 (~L960): takes the best favour action only
  when its score is `> 1` — i.e. effectively only the `rep→coins` fallback. A
  `coins→rep` action is therefore **never** taken (score `1`).
- `competitiveFavourScore` (~L1981) encodes the **same** stalled+buffer rule for
  `CompetitiveGreedyStrategy`; its priority chain likewise takes favour only
  when `score > 1` (~L2145).

**Why the current gate is too loose.** `getCheapestMarketCost` includes *every*
market family (staff/events included) and the reward of the placement is not
considered at all. A stalled AI will exchange 200 reputation for 300 coins even
when the only affordable card is value-negative (e.g. Pawn Shop, which carries
`reputationPerTurn = -10`) or has no synergy.

**Measured current behaviour (60-seed intake sample, greedy, commit `dev` HEAD
at intake time).** The AI takes `rep→coins` several times per run and never
takes `coins→rep`:

| Difficulty | `rep→coins` uses/run | `coins→rep` uses/run | win rate | rep-collapse / bankruptcy losses |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Easy   | 3.52 | 0 | 0.650 | 15 / 6 |
| Medium | 3.12 | 0 | 0.350 | 29 / 10 |
| Hard   | 2.18 | 0 | 0.117 | 26 / 27 |

**Loss condition.** Reputation collapse fires when
`resourceBank.reputation <= 0` after turn 1
(`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`).

**Existing tests.** `tests/main-street/community-favour-ai.test.ts` currently
pins the *old* contract, including
`scores coins-to-rep at the low default` and
`scores rep-to-coins above the default when cash-strapped with rep to spare`, so
it must be updated alongside the heuristic (AC6).

## Desired change

Replace the "stalled + any buffer" `rep→coins` heuristic with an
**enablement + value/timing** heuristic: exchange reputation for coins only when
the coins buy a **profitable** placement **and** the placement's reward (income
+ synergy over the remaining horizon) is **significant enough, early enough**
(e.g. securing a strong synergy slot) to justify the reputation spent. Keep the
reputation-buffer guard. Apply the same rule to the competitive mirror so the
two heuristics cannot diverge.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — `scoreAction` `community-favour` case, the
  `rep→coins` enablement/value helper, `chooseGreedyAction` Priority 9,
  and `competitiveFavourScore` (competitive mirror).
- `tests/main-street/community-favour-ai.test.ts` — update existing contract
  tests and add the new enablement/value/timing cases.
- `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-greedy-guardrail.test.ts` — design-intent
  win-rate ladder / loss-mode guard (extend only if the loss-mode assertion
  already exists there).
- `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts` — committed-baseline
  tolerances (regression guard; no change expected unless drift is intended).
- `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md` — document the revised Community Favour
  move-evaluation heuristic.
- `docs/main-street/` — new or updated before/after evidence artefact.
- `src/scripts/balance/engine/global-metrics.ts` — loss-mode decomposition (G5),
  if a reputation-collapse metric needs surfacing for the evidence artefact.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE** — R2: re-tune reputation sources for the slower-coin
  economy (open, `plan_complete`, producer question pending). **Coordinates:**
  R2 tunes card-data reputation values to move the Medium loss-mode split into
  the PRD band; this item changes *AI decision quality* and must not double-count
  the same outcome. R2's implementation comment explicitly measured that
  `favourCoinsToRepCost` tuning does not move greedy behaviour — corroborating
  that this fix belongs in the AI heuristic.
- **MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3** — parent of R2: five-turn payback rebalance
  (in-progress). Source of the tighter-economy design intent.
- **MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5** — R4: re-price community spaces and events (completed);
  touches community-space reputation pricing — out of scope here.
- **MS-0MUACDDMX004KWY8** — "Bank your spare action is a dead end in the
  tutorial" (open): also concerns the `rep→coins` fallback as a stall-breaker.
- **CG-0MSTOATDQ005XDET** — original Community Favour implementation (free
  once-per-turn exchange) and the `avgCoinsPerTurn` guardrail widening that
  recorded the `rep→coins` fallback's liquidity contribution.
- **CG-0MT3JMGA60091J8W** — BankingGreedyStrategy: introduces
  `aiPlanningHorizon`, the horizon helper this heuristic will reuse, and the
  precedent for difficulty-scaled AI aggressiveness.
- **MS-0MUWKG6NS006OG2D** — "Community Garden should be Entertainment"
  (completed): community-space card data (context only).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — stall/win-rate regression.** Removing the free fallback means more
  end-turns when the AI cannot afford a profitable card. This is the intended
  trade-off, but Medium/Hard win rates could fall; the ladder and committed
  tolerances must still hold (AC5). Mitigation: measure before/after and treat
  any out-of-tolerance drift as a producer decision.
- **Risk — threshold over-fitting.** A value/timing threshold tuned to the
  200-seed canonical set may not generalise. Mitigation: keep it a single named
  constant, document its derivation, and pin behaviour with unit tests rather
  than only the stochastic guardrail.
- **Risk — overlap with R2.** R2 also targets the reputation-collapse share of
  losses; changing both at once confounds attribution. Mitigation: this item's
  primary ACs are behavioural (usage + enablement), and any loss-mode claim is
  reported alongside R2's state rather than asserted as this item's alone.
- **Risk — competitive divergence.** If only the single-player heuristic is
  changed, `competitiveFavourScore` keeps the loose rule. Mitigation: apply the
  shared helper to both (decision recorded as an assumption below).
- **Risk — scope creep.** Do not rebalance Community Favour parameters, cards,
  or the collapse threshold; record extra opportunities as linked work items.
- **Assumption.** Scope is the greedy AI heuristic (single-player
  `scoreAction`); the competitive mirror is updated with the same helper to
  prevent divergence, but competitive-specific tuning is out of scope.
- **Assumption.** "Profitable card" means a legal placement whose greedy score
  (`scoreBusinessAction` / `scorePlayBusinessFromHandAction`, value − effective
  cost) is `> 0` after the exchange.
- **Assumption.** "Early brings significant value" is represented by
  `aiPlanningHorizon(state)` and the projected synergy bonus — the same horizon
  helper the banking heuristic uses.
- **Assumption.** Canonical profile = 200 seeds, prefix `mc-balance`, 60 max
  turns, greedy, Easy/Medium/Hard.
- **Assumption.** The committed baseline is regenerated only via the
  drift-report-then-ask workflow with producer approval.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No blocking producer questions were required — the seed intent is specific and
the remaining decisions were resolved by repo research and a measurement run.
Records (for auditability; idempotent, do not duplicate on re-run):

- Q: Does "using Community Favour to get money" mean `rep→coins` or
  `coins→rep`? — Answer (research): `rep→coins` (200 reputation → 300 coins).
  Measured 60-seed greedy sample shows `rep→coins` used 2.18–3.52×/run and
  `coins→rep` used 0×; only `rep→coins` drains the loss-causing resource.
  Source: `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` `scoreAction`; intake evidence script.
- Q: Is the fix a parameter re-tune (like R2) or an AI-heuristic change? —
  Answer (research): AI-heuristic. R2's implementation comment records that
  reducing `favourCoinsToRepCost` to 10/20/50/100 moved the Medium loss split by
  <2 pp — parameters do not move greedy behaviour. Source: MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE
  implementation comment.
- Q: What is a "profitable card"? — Answer (research): a legal placement whose
  greedy score (income + projected synergy over `aiPlanningHorizon`, minus
  effective cost) is positive. Source: `scoreBusinessAction`,
  `scorePlayBusinessFromHandAction`, `aiPlanningHorizon` in
  `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`.
- Q: Should the competitive AI heuristic change too? — Answer (producer):
  **yes** — both `scoreAction` and `competitiveFavourScore` encode the same
  stalled+buffer rule; apply the shared enablement/value helper to both (via a
  common function) to avoid divergence. Competitive-specific tuning remains out
  of scope. Source: producer reply, 2026-10-06.
- Q: Should this item target the PRD loss-mode band (rep collapse 20–40% of
  Medium losses) as a hard gate? — Answer (producer): **no** — the primary gate
  is behavioural (usage/enablement) plus the win-rate ladder and
  committed-baseline tolerances; the loss-mode band remains owned by R2
  (MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE) via card-data, and changing both confounds attribution.
  Source: producer reply, 2026-10-06.

### Questions resolved

Both producer questions were answered on 2026-10-06: (1) competitive mirror —
**yes**, apply the shared helper; (2) loss-mode band hard gate — **no**. No open
questions remain.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MTV9AS15004AC1E** – Visual representation of reputation (open)
- **MS-0MUWE6NCA008LDXM** – Two-column Game Over overlay (completed)
- **MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E** – Assign dedicated card art to every Main Street card (1024×1024 source; eliminate generic Fallback art) (open)
